acts.22.p1.b1.text: “Brothers and fathers, listen now to my defense before you.”

acts.22.p1.b2.text: When they heard him speak to them in Hebrew, they became even more silent. Then Paul declared,

acts.22.p1.b3.text: “I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but raised in this city. I was educated at the feet of Gamaliel in strict conformity to the law of our fathers.

acts.22.p1.b4.text: I am just as zealous for God as any of you here today.

acts.22.p2.b5.text: I persecuted this Way even to the death, detaining both men and women and throwing them into prison,

acts.22.p2.b6.text: … the high priest and the whole Council can testify about me.

acts.22.p2.b7.text: I even obtained letters from them to their brothers in Damascus, and I was on my way to apprehend these people and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.

acts.22.p3.b8.text: About noon as I was approaching Damascus,

acts.22.p3.b9.text: suddenly a bright light from heaven flashed around me. I fell to the ground and heard a voice say to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?’

acts.22.p3.b11.text: ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting,’ He replied.

acts.22.p4.b12.text: My companions saw the light, but they could not understand the voice of the One speaking to me.

acts.22.p4.b13.text: Then I asked, ‘What should I do, Lord?’

acts.22.p4.b14.text: ‘Get up and go into Damascus,’ He told me. ‘There you will be told all that you have been appointed to do.’

acts.22.p4.b15.text: Because the brilliance of the light had blinded me, my companions led me by the hand into Damascus.

acts.22.p5.b16.text: There a man named Ananias, a devout observer of the law who was highly regarded by all the Jews living there,

acts.22.p5.b17.text: came and stood beside me. ‘Brother Saul,’ he said, ‘receive your sight.’ And at that moment I could see him.

acts.22.p5.b18.text: Then he said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you … You will be His witness to everyone of what you have seen and heard.

acts.22.p5.b19.text: And now what are you waiting for? Get up, be baptized, and wash your sins away, calling on His name.’

acts.22.p6.b20.text: Later, when I had returned to Jerusalem and was praying at the temple, I fell into a trance

acts.22.p6.b21.text: and saw the Lord saying to me, ‘Hurry! Leave Jerusalem quickly, because the people here will not accept your testimony about Me.’

acts.22.p6.b22.text: ‘Lord,’ I answered, ‘they know very well that in one synagogue after another I imprisoned and beat those who believed in You.

acts.22.p6.b23.text: And when the blood of Your witness Stephen was shed, I stood there giving my approval and watching over the garments of those who killed him.’

acts.22.p7.b24.text: Then He said to me, ‘Go! I will send you far away to the Gentiles.’”

acts.22.p7.b25.text: “Rid the earth of him! He is not fit to live!”

acts.22.p7.b26.text: As they were shouting and throwing off their cloaks and tossing dust into the air,

acts.22.p8.b27.text: … the commander ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks. He directed that Paul be flogged and interrogated …

acts.22.p8.b28.text: But as they stretched him out to strap him down,

acts.22.p8.b29.text: “Is it lawful for you to flog a Roman citizen without a trial?”

acts.22.p9.b30.text: “What are you going to do?” … “This man is a Roman citizen.”

acts.22.p9.b31.text: “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?”

acts.22.p9.b33.text: “I paid a high price for my citizenship,”

acts.22.p10.b35.text: The next day the commander, wanting to learn the real reason Paul was accused by the Jews, released him

acts.22.p10.b36.text: … ordered the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin to assemble.

acts.22.p10.b37.text: Then he brought Paul down and had him stand before them.
